stream and channel lifetime (section 13.1): a Write / Listen stream classifies its opening metadata once and is decided as soon as its first request names the database, then stays admitted for its whole life; a WebChannel classifies the opening init header block the same way, binds the channel to the admitted app and the session epoch of that admission, and closes the channel when a later envelope presents a replacement token for another app or one that does not verify. Neither token expiry nor a policy change ends an admitted stream: reconnecting is a new admission

resumable upload binding (section 13.2): an enforced initiation records the admitted app and the epoch of that admission in the upload session, and every later request on that session -- continuation, status query, cancel and finalization -- must present a valid token for the same app. A refused request is refused before the command is read, so it neither advances nor deletes the upload; token expiry mid-upload therefore preserves the resumable state
off is the absence of a policy, so a service configured off structurally cannot parse a header or record an observation

the explicit bypass matrix of specification section 12.2, each surface requiring its own credential and never a path shape: the Firestore owner credential, Identity Toolkit Admin routes with the owner credential, the emulator inspection routes with the control token, the Storage JSON API dialect with the owner credential, and a Storage download URL whose token binds in constant time to the resolved bucket, object name and generation

denial before Security Rules and before every side effect: no user, no issued or rotated credential, no consumed OOB or phone code, no MFA change, no object generation, no upload session, no Firestore mutation and no rules document-access budget consumption

the error contract of section 17: PERMISSION_DENIED with the public code in fireemu-code metadata on gRPC, HTTP 403 Google JSON on Firestore REST and on Auth, and the Firebase Storage JSON error envelope with 403 on Storage; the public code is APP_CHECK_REQUIRED or APP_CHECK_INVALID and never the detailed reason

duplicate IDs refused, duplicate shapes warned (FS_TEXT_DUPLICATE_INDEX_DEFINITION, field-order insensitive, apiScope aware), unresolved language override warned, unsupported, unknown (at every level) and output-only fields (index.state) refused
notes: Enterprise edition only
unimplemented: backfill lifecycle (advanceBackfill, completeBackfill, failBuild, repair answer UNIMPLEMENTED without changing state; FS-TEXT-IDX-1)
posting data and local search (Milestone G)

notes: serializable: read sets and executed queries are re-validated at commit
conformance: firestore/transaction-read-set-abort (conformance/README.md); this records agreement with the official Local Emulator Suite, never with production
WebChannel v8 transport of the browser web SDK (Listen / Write) on the Firestore port; resume as in FS-LSN-1

a target refused on its own merits, including one that rides along with the opening handshake, is delivered as TargetChange REMOVE through the first back channel and the session stays open; only a stream-level error closes it

implemented: get / create / update / delete against the returned snapshot or the staged commit
list / aggregation / Listen queries proven from equality, in, !=, not-in, array-contains(-any) and inequality (range) constraints plus request.query.limit / offset / orderBy (RULES-QUERY-CONSTRAINTS)
get() / exists() / getAfter() (getAfter over the state the whole commit leaves behind; fails closed on reads and query proofs)

the string, list, map, set, path, timestamp, duration, latlng, math and hashing surfaces, map.diff() and its key sets, range indexing (x[i:j]), path.bind(), and the int / float / string / path conversions
collection groups need a recursive wildcard rule
notes: the language is measured rather than assumed: conformance/src/rules-probe installs the same bounded Rules programs into the pinned official Firestore emulator and into fireemu and compares every verdict (680 claims in conformance/rules-matrix.json, 22 whole-program probes in conformance/rules-programs.json)
query proofs are sound, not complete: a rule that reads an unconstrained field denies the query

the principal request.auth is built from follows the compatibility profile on both the Firestore and the Storage Rules surfaces (see AUTH-RULES-1); the rules themselves are evaluated identically under both profiles

request.query.orderBy is a map from field path to "ASC" / "DESC", request.query.limit is null without a limit, and request.resource and request.query are absent rather than null on a request that has neither

string.matches() / replace(): the RE2 surface the official runtime has -- capturing groups with $0 / $1 expansion, the inline flags (?i) (?s) (?m), POSIX and Unicode classes, hex escapes -- and, as in RE2, no lookarounds and no backreferences; a literal pattern is compiled while the ruleset is, so an unusable one fails the load
a recursive call and a call chain of more than twenty calls are compile errors, with the official compiler's messages
three language rows are documented divergences, all the same one: the official compiler's static type checker rejects at load what fireemu raises at evaluation; the request decision is the same
conformance: firestore/rules-decisions (conformance/README.md); this records agreement with the official Local Emulator Suite, never with production

implemented: RULES-EXPRESSIONS-PER-REQUEST 1000
RULES-FUNCTION-CALL-DEPTH 20 calls (a chain of 21 functions is the deepest that compiles), refused when the ruleset loads
RULES-RECURSION 0: a recursive or cyclical call is refused when the ruleset loads
RULES-DOC-ACCESS-SINGLE 10 per operation and per query proof (get, exists and getAfter of one path each count once)
RULES-DOC-ACCESS-MULTI-TOTAL 20 across atomic commits and BatchGetDocuments
notes: each number is measured against the pinned official emulator, not read off the documentation: ten document accesses are served and eleven are denied, thirty accesses of one path are served, and the call-depth boundary is the one its compiler reports (conformance/rules-programs.json)

implemented: GET /emulator/v1/projects/{project}:ruleCoverage on the Firestore port: the loaded rules files, then a report of one tree per allow condition and per function body, each node naming its sourcePosition (line, column, currentOffset, endOffset) and the values it took with a count each
GET /emulator/v1/projects/{project}:ruleCoverage.html: the same document as a page that underlines every evaluated expression and shows its values on hover
PUT /emulator/v1/projects/{project}:securityRules: the official load route, answering 200 with issues or 400 whose message names the rejected position as L<line>:<column>
GET /v1/sessions/{session}/rules/requests on the control API: the last 100 decided requests, newest first, each with its decision and what every expression evaluated to
the Emulator UI's Rules page lists the decided requests and expands one into its per-expression trace, reading the same control route
notes: an expression that raised is reported as undefined carrying the innermost expression that raised and its message; an expression nothing reached has children and no values, as the official report does
the coverage and the traces live with the ruleset they describe, so loading another one replaces both and no stale position is ever served

the two emulator routes take no credential, because the official ones take none and @firebase/rules-unit-testing calls them with no headers; both are loopback-only and both echo the values the ruleset computed, which is what a coverage report is
the control route carries the control token like every privileged route, and never carries a token, a signature or any claim other than the subject the rule saw as request.auth.uid

the denial message fireemu returns is its own: the official emulator answers PERMISSION_DENIED with a per-allow trace of its evaluation, which is a diagnostic rather than an API contract, and fireemu publishes the same information through these routes instead

implemented: Firebase Storage protocol (/v0/b, X-Goog-Upload resumable, download tokens)
JSON API (/storage/v1, /upload/storage/v1, /download/storage/v1, emulator-style /b paths, Content-Range resumable, rewriteTo)
generation / metageneration preconditions (match / not-match / source)
generation selectors (current generation only)
prefix / delimiter listing
MD5 / CRC32C (X-Goog-Hash verified before commit)
Range: bytes=a-b / a- / -n
notes: Storage object triggers are not part of this entry: FN-EVT-1 delivers object finalized / deleted / metadataUpdated events, and this entry owns the object surface only
objects are at most 256 MiB and request bodies at most 260 MiB (413 beyond that)
upload bytes are moved into the object store, never copied: one payload-sized buffer per upload
request bodies buffered at the same time are admitted against a process-wide 1 GiB budget; an upload that does not fit is refused with 503 and Retry-After: 1
conformance: storage/admin-upload-download-metadata, storage/client-protocol-and-rules (conformance/README.md); this records agreement with the official Local Emulator Suite, never with production
unimplemented: object versioning / archived generations
ACLs and signed URLs
compose
notifications

implemented: service firebase.storage: get / list / create / update / delete with request.resource and resource
resumable uploads are authorized at finalization with the received bytes
list requires rules_version 2
Firebase protocol goes through the rules; the JSON API is a privileged surface unless an end-user token is presented
firestore.get() / firestore.exists() over the latest Firestore state of the project (STORAGE-RULES-FIRESTORE-ACCESS: two per request)
notes: a JSON API rewrite with an end-user token evaluates the source read and the destination write as two requests, each with its own two-call budget
conformance: storage/client-protocol-and-rules (conformance/README.md); this records agreement with the official Local Emulator Suite, never with production

implemented: firebase.json for every served product: firestore in object or array (named-database) form with rules and indexes (also the legacy index spelling), storage in object or array form with target / bucket / rules, functions in object or array (multi-codebase) form with source, codebase, runtime and ignore
emulators.<name>.host and .port for firestore, auth, storage, functions, hub and ui, emulators.ui.enabled, and emulators.singleProjectMode
loopback-only hosts: a routable emulators.<name>.host is refused rather than exposing a product to the network
.firebaserc project aliases: --project resolves an alias, falls back to the default alias, and takes an unknown value as a project ID exactly as firebase --project does
--config reads either file: one carrying schemaVersion is the fireemu canonical configuration, anything else is a firebase.json, so `firebase emulators:exec --config firebase.json` works verbatim
unknown keys fail closed at every level of the sections fireemu reads
an emulators.<name> entry for a product fireemu does not serve is an error when --only named that product and a notice otherwise; nothing is silently dropped
spec/config/firebase-json.schema.json with a valid and an invalid corpus, checked by tools/config-schema-check and replayed through the loader by a unit test
unimplemented: a named Firestore database serves, but its own rules and indexes are not loaded (only the (default) entry's are); the daemon says so
one Storage ruleset covers every bucket, so a per-target rules file is reported and not loaded
one Functions codebase runs per daemon: a multi-codebase project names it with --only functions:<codebase>
emulators.singleProjectMode is recorded and published but enforces nothing on its own: fireemu isolates every project into its own session, which is stricter
hosting, database and the other deferred products are not parsed beyond reporting them
notes: command-line ports override firebase.json; firebase.json overrides the canonical configuration

implemented: --only decides the lifecycle: an unselected Firestore, Storage or Functions binds no listener at all and its port stays free for whatever else wants it

the child environment carries exactly the canonical variables of the selected services, in the firebase-tools@15.28.2 env.ts formats: FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST and FIREBASE_FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_ADDRESS as host:port, FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST as host:port, FIREBASE_STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST as host:port next to STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST as http://host:port, FIREBASE_EMULATOR_HUB as host:port, and a synthesised FIREBASE_CONFIG
the variables of unselected services are removed from the command environment, so a stale value in the shell cannot point a suite at a service this run is not serving
an official service fireemu does not serve (database, hosting, apphosting, pubsub, eventarc, tasks, dataconnect, extensions) is refused by --only with its scope status before anything binds
--only functions:<codebase> selects one codebase, as the official CLI spells it
the functions runner sees the same selection: an unselected product leaves its variable unset there too
notes: there is no CLOUD_STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST variable: the firebase-tools constant of that name emits STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST, and fireemu sets that one
FIREBASE_DATABASE_EMULATOR_HOST is never set, because fireemu serves no Realtime Database; it is cleared from the child environment for the same reason

two published divergences from the official CLI: fireemu also sets GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT (the official CLI sets only GCLOUD_PROJECT), and it clears the variables of unselected services where the official CLI only adds

the Identity Toolkit socket also carries the control API, the App Check exchange and the UI API; when auth is not selected the control plane moves to an ephemeral loopback port and the configured Auth port is left free

implemented: the Emulator Hub on the official default port 4400 (emulators.hub, --hub-port, daemon.hubPort), best effort like the UI port: a busy default disables discovery, a busy explicit port is an error, and --hub-port 0 turns it off

GET /emulators: an object keyed by official emulator name, each entry carrying name, host, port, pid and the listen specs, with the Hub and the UI listed as upstream lists them; only services that actually bound a listener appear
GET /: the locator (version, origins, pid) plus this listener's host and port
PUT /functions/disableBackgroundTriggers and PUT /functions/enableBackgroundTriggers answering the official enabled body, or 400 when no functions codebase is loaded

the locator file <temp dir>/hub-<project>.json written at start with version, origins and pid, and removed at exit only while it still names this process; a live locator from another suite is left alone with a notice
FIREBASE_EMULATOR_HUB exported to the exec command as a bare host:port

@firebase/rules-unit-testing 5.0.2 discovers the suite with no explicit host: tools/sdk-smoke/rules-unit-testing.mjs runs initializeTestEnvironment with an empty configuration and exercises the rules decisions, withSecurityRulesDisabled, clearFirestore and a trigger-suppressed write
DELETE /emulator/v1/projects/{project}/databases/{database}/documents on the Firestore port, which is what clearFirestore() calls

POST /_admin/export with the official body {"path", "initiatedBy"}, refusing a request that carries an Origin header exactly as upstream does; it is what fireemu emulators:export drives after finding the suite through its locator file
PUT /emulator/v1/projects/{project}:securityRules on the Firestore port, which is what loading rules from a test environment calls (see RULES-DIAG-1)
unimplemented: POST /dataconnect/clearData: fireemu serves no Data Connect emulator
notes: the Hub answers loopback Host headers only, which the official Hub does not check; it can disable background triggers, so a page on a routable name must not reach it by DNS rebinding

a suite moving from the official emulator has to do two things until the Auth gaps close: state an iat on the token authenticatedContext mints (createMockUserToken defaults to iat 0, so exp is 3600 and the token expired in 1970, which fireemu's virtual clock refuses) and create the users the contexts stand for, because fireemu resolves an ID token subject against the project Auth store

implemented: emulators:start and emulators:exec as exact aliases of up and exec, and emulators:export <dir> [--project <id>] [--force] against a running suite
the official flag names --only, --project / -P, --config, --import, --export-on-exit, --inspect-functions and --log-verbosity, next to the fireemu port flags

--inspect-functions [port] inserts Node's --inspect=<port> before the runner script (default 9229), and refuses with a precise message when a configured functions.runner is not Node rather than starting without the inspector
--log-verbosity quiet | info | debug (case-insensitive): quiet suppresses the banner and the notices, debug adds the resolved configuration

exit codes: the command's own status from exec, 128 + signal when a signal ended it, 1 for a startup failure or a refused configuration, 2 for a usage error; a refusal never starts a listener and never runs the command
SIGINT and SIGTERM are forwarded to the command with their identity and the whole process group is swept afterwards
unimplemented: --ui / --no-ui: the UI is controlled by --ui-port and emulators.ui
notes: the official CLI takes the script as a positional argument; fireemu takes it after -- so no shell quoting is needed

implemented: the Hub background-trigger switch: disabling drops Firestore, Storage, Pub/Sub and Auth events instead of holding them, so re-enabling delivers nothing retroactively, which is what the official emulator does (its background-trigger route answers 204 and discards the body)
HTTP and callable invocations, manual functions/{name}:run requests and virtual-clock schedule runs keep working while background triggers are disabled: none of them is a data-change delivery
events already accepted keep their place in the outbox and are still delivered and retried, as upstream drains the work queue it had already taken on
unimplemented: the Logging emulator stream (the official port 4500) is out of scope for this release: an emulators.logging entry is reported and nothing is served on that port. The functions log stream the UI consumes lives on the control API instead (GET /v1/sessions/{s}/functions)
notes: the switch is process-wide, not per session: one functions runtime serves every session

implemented: the pinned firebase-export-metadata.json manifest of firebase-tools 15.28.2: the version, the per-product sections with their version, path and (Firestore) metadata_file, in the official product order

the Firestore managed export the emulator jar writes: the LevelDB log framing with its masked CRC-32C, and the apphosting.datastore.v3 EntityProto encoding of a document, covering null, boolean, integer (two's complement), double (exact bits, so NaN and negative zero survive), string, bytes, microsecond timestamps, geo points, references, maps, arrays, the empty array as an indexed EMPTY_LIST property, the empty map as a nested EntityProto, and paths of any subcollection depth

auth_export/accounts.json as the identitytoolkit#DownloadAccountResponse the CLI streams to disk, with providers, custom claims, phone second factors, the reversible fakeHash:salt=<salt>:password=<plaintext> convention and auth_export/config.json
storage_export/buckets.json, blobs/<id> and metadata/<id>.json, with the object bytes byte for byte and the recorded generation, metageneration, times, hashes, download tokens and custom metadata
a member the model does not know is carried through an import and written out again unchanged, so a newer emulator's field is never silently dropped
a malformed section is refused with the byte offset or the member that caused it, never read short
unimplemented: database_export (Realtime Database) and dataconnect_export (SQL Connect) are detected and refused with their deferred status; fireemu serves neither product
accounts-<tenant>.json is refused: fireemu serves no Identity Platform tenants, and importing only the default tenant would drop accounts
a passwordHash that is not the emulator's own reversible form (a real scrypt hash from a production export) is refused rather than installed as a credential nothing can sign in with
notes: the format is pinned by fixtures recorded from real runs of the official suite (crates/fireemu/tests/fixtures/export/, recorded by conformance/src/record-export.mjs)
the official managed export records no document creation or update time, so an import necessarily stamps them with the commit that installs them; the official Firestore emulator does the same

a Firestore database other than (default) has no place in the official format, whose export request is hard-coded to databases/(default); fireemu writes those under a fireemu member of the manifest that the official CLI ignores
a TOTP second factor has no official equivalent (the Auth emulator has no TOTP factor at all) and is written under totpInfo.sharedSecretKey

implemented: --import <dir> reads every section of the products --only selected into memory and installs them together under the exclusive admission barrier, so a failure in any product leaves the empty start state and exits 1 naming the product and the path
a section of a product --only did not select is skipped with a notice rather than refused

--export-on-exit [dir] writes the export on a clean exit, on the command's failure and on SIGINT or SIGTERM; an omitted directory resolves to the --import one, and the working directory or a parent is refused

emulators:export <dir> finds the running suite through its Emulator Hub locator file and drives POST /_admin/export, whose body is the official {"path", "initiatedBy"} and which refuses a request carrying an Origin header
overwrite protection: a directory is overwritten only when it is empty or already holds a firebase-export-metadata.json
every exported directory is created 0700 and every file 0600, because an Auth export carries password material and TOTP secrets
an import fires no Auth user event and no Storage object event: it restores state rather than producing it
unimplemented: importing a project id other than the one the run serves installs the data under the project the artifact names, with a notice, rather than remapping it
notes: fireemu's own session snapshots, fault plans, text index definitions and every App Check secret (debug tokens, project epochs, the instance signing key) never reach an export directory

a password set through fireemu's own API has no reversible emulator form and is exported without a passwordHash rather than with an invented one; a password that arrived from an official import is written back exactly as it was read

implemented: every exported function the runner cannot serve is reported, never dropped: the manifest carries an `ignored` array with the name, region, trigger family and product scope, GET .../functions publishes it, and the daemon prints one `functions[<region>-<name>]: function ignored (<family>): <reason>` line per entry
an export whose endpoint cannot be described -- a v1 provider whose lazily-computed __endpoint throws -- becomes one ignored record naming it rather than a dead runner
export order is the codebase's, not the ES module namespace's alphabetical order, so the emulator lists functions the way the official one does
every codebase declared in a firebase.json `functions` array is loaded, one runner process per codebase, behind one runtime and one functions port; --only functions:<codebase> selects one
a function name two codebases both export is refused, naming both
`source`, `codebase`, `runtime` and `ignore` are read; a codebase whose runtime is not nodejs* is refused with the language named
unimplemented: Python (functions-framework) and Dart loader paths: refused by name, never handed to node
hot reload of a codebase's source: a change needs a restart, and `ignore` is recorded rather than driving a watcher
notes: a trigger family belonging to a product fireemu does not serve fails discovery by default, naming every such function; functions.unservedTriggers = "report" asks for the official emulator's carry-on instead, which prints the line and starts anyway

the official emulator never fails on an unsupported export: it logs `Unsupported trigger` (DEBUG) or `Unsupported function type on <name>` (WARN) and records the definition with ignored: true. fireemu keeps that inventory and parts company only on the product decision

implemented: the dotenv chain in the official order and dialect (firebase-tools lib/functions/env.js): .env, .env.<projectId>, .env.<alias>, and emulator-only .env.local, later files overriding earlier ones

the official refusals, with their sentences: both a projectId and an alias file present, a line that is not an assignment, a reserved key, a key that is not SCREAMING_SNAKE, a key under a reserved prefix
the official quoting: single-quoted literal, double-quoted expanding \n \r \t \v \\ \' \", unquoted ending at the first #, and a quoted value allowed to cross lines
.secret.local for defineSecret parameters, parsed the same way and merged over the chain
.runtimeconfig.json passed through as CLOUD_RUNTIME_CONFIG; a malformed one is reported and treated as absent

the variables the official emulator gives a runtime: FIREBASE_CONFIG (storageBucket, databaseURL, projectId), GCLOUD_PROJECT, GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT, FUNCTIONS_EMULATOR, K_REVISION, PORT, TZ=UTC, METADATA_SERVER_DETECTION, plus per-invocation FUNCTION_TARGET, FUNCTION_SIGNATURE_TYPE and K_SERVICE

defineString / defineInt / defineBoolean / defineList / defineSecret resolve from that environment with the official missing-parameter behaviour, which is the SDK's: the emulator resolves no parameters and prompts for nothing
unimplemented: Google Cloud Secret Manager as a fallback for a secret .secret.local does not carry: fireemu holds no credentials and makes no network call, so the parameter resolves as an unset variable does
notes: the pinned firebase-functions@7.3.2 has removed functions.config(); CLOUD_RUNTIME_CONFIG is still set, as the official emulator sets it, and no supported SDK surface reads it

FUNCTION_TARGET, FUNCTION_SIGNATURE_TYPE and K_SERVICE name the most recently started invocation: the official emulator runs one runtime process per trigger and can set them once, and one fireemu runner serves a whole codebase
fireemu also sets GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, which the official emulator does not; the Google client libraries read either name
